title: Hell Bunny Celeste Trousers and an Apron Belly: Size for Depth, Not the D-Rings
summary: The Celeste trousers combine a high waist, front pleats, side adjusters, and only slight stretch. Here is how to judge whether the cut has enough front depth before accepting a merely adjustable waistband.
author: Curvy& Editorial

sections.heading: The real question is where the trousers make room
paragraphs: A September r/PlusSizeFashion question about Hell Bunny's Celeste trousers focused on a problem that a waist measurement cannot answer: how a high-waisted, pleated trouser will sit over an apron belly without bunching. That is a front-depth question. Two people can share the same waist and hip measurements while needing very different amounts of fabric between the waistband and crotch.

The official Celeste description confirms a high waist, wide leg, two front pleats, a center-front zip and button, and D-ring adjusters at both sides. Those details can create a polished vintage line, but they also make waistband position and rise more consequential than they would be in a soft pull-on pant. The community post is one shopper's fit concern, not proof that the style works or fails for a particular body shape.

sections.heading: Side adjusters refine the waist; they do not create belly room
paragraphs: The D-rings can take in a waistband that is slightly loose. They cannot add front rise, lengthen the crotch curve, or supply more room through the lower stomach and seat. If the trousers pull upward under the belly, form horizontal tension lines across the front, or make the back waistband dip when the front sits correctly, loosening the adjusters will not solve the underlying geometry.

Front pleats are not automatically extra belly capacity either. A pleat that hangs closed while standing and opens gently when sitting is doing useful work. A pleat that is already pulled flat or forced open at rest is signaling that its allowance has been consumed. This reading is an editorial fit diagnostic, not a measurement published by Hell Bunny.

sections.heading: Use both waist and hip, then respect the slight stretch
paragraphs: Hell Bunny describes the fabric as 63% polyester, 34% viscose, and 3% elastane with slight stretch. The brand instructs shoppers to follow both waist and hip measurements and to size up when between sizes. On its body chart, 2XL is listed at a 36.4-inch waist and 47.4-inch hip; 3XL at 39.4 and 50.4; 4XL at 42.3 and 53.3; 5XL at 45.3 and 56.3; and 6XL at 48.2 and 59.3.

Choose the size required by the more demanding measurement rather than sizing to the waist and expecting the adjusters to compensate everywhere else. For an apron belly, measure at the place where the waistband is intended to sit, then take the fullest hip measurement without compressing the front. If those measurements point to different sizes, preserving hip and front-body room is the safer starting test; the side tabs may then recover modest waist ease.

sections.heading: The missing measurements matter as much as the published ones
paragraphs: Hell Bunny's chart supplies body measurements, not the Celeste's finished garment waist, hip, front rise, back rise, or thigh. The product page publishes a 75-centimeter, or 29.5-inch, inseam for size small, but it does not say how that measurement grades through the plus sizes. A shopper deciding whether the waistband will clear the fullest part of the stomach still lacks the most useful dimensions.

Before paying international return postage, ask customer service for the laid-flat garment waist at the loosest adjuster setting, hip measured below the waistband, front and back rise, and thigh width in the exact size being considered. Compare the rises and hip circumference with a non-stretch woven trouser that already sits well. A favorite legging or elastic-waist pant is a poor reference because its fabric and closure solve fit differently.

sections.heading: Test the seated fit before deciding
paragraphs: Try the trousers with the adjusters fully relaxed first. The waistband should close without pulling the front pleats open, and the center-front zip should remain flat rather than bowing. Sit upright, lean forward, lift a knee, and walk. Watch for pressure under the stomach, a crotch seam that is pulled forward, gaping at the back waist, or pleats that never return after standing.

Only after the front and seat have enough room should you tighten the side tabs. If one size gives adequate depth but leaves too much waist even at the tabs' tightest position, tailoring the waistband may be more successful than sizing down into a shallow rise. Hell Bunny accepts eligible returns within 30 days of delivery, but it does not offer free returns or direct exchanges; the customer pays to return the first pair and places a new order for another size. That makes a measurement request worthwhile before the first order.
bullets: Prioritize the size that fits the fuller of your waist or hip measurements.
Read permanently opened pleats and front drag lines as signs to test more room.
Treat the D-rings as waist fine-tuning, not a substitute for adequate rise and hip depth.

researchNote: This guide responds to a September 2026 community fit question and verifies the Celeste's construction, fabric, chart, and return terms on Hell Bunny's official site. The discussion describes an individual concern; the front-depth and pleat diagnostics are editorial interpretation based on garment construction.
